title: Economic Outlook - Top-Down Macro Schema
description: Structure for a standing 'Economic Outlook' workstream, modeled on the mock-FOMC format used in the College Fed Challenge (see fed_challenge_dataset.json for worked examples). This is the top layer of a top-down pipeline: it produces a regime read and a set of trading parameters that the per-ticker research workflow consumes, rather than re-deriving a macro view per ticker.

meta.description: Versioning info. Every refresh is a new snapshot, never an overwrite -- this is what makes the scorecard log possible later.

refresh_reason.description: Why this version exists. Ad hoc refreshes should be rare -- if you're refreshing weekly 'just because,' the cadence is wrong.

next_scheduled_refresh.description: Default: next FOMC meeting date. Full narrative refresh cadence should track the 8/year FOMC schedule; the glance layer updates continuously between refreshes.

regime_tag.description: The single most-referenced field in the whole document -- this is what the ticker-level workflow reads first. Keep it short and stable between refreshes; if it changes every version, it isn't a regime, it's noise.

label.description: One-line regime name, e.g. 'late-cycle, disinflationary, easing bias, r-star elevated'

dual_mandate_balance.description: Which side of the mandate is currently binding, e.g. 'labor risk now dominates inflation risk' -- this should read like the risk-balance line at the end of a Fed Challenge presentation.

growth_and_financial_conditions.description: GDP/potential, r-star, credit spreads, NFCI, valuations -- whatever tells you if policy is actually restrictive/accommodative in practice, not just on paper.

house_view_path.description: Your own forward rate-path call, stated as explicitly as a mock-FOMC vote (e.g. '-25bp next meeting, hold after').

market_implied_path.description: What futures/OIS pricing currently implies. Always state this alongside the house view -- the gap between the two is usually the actual trade.

gap_analysis.description: Why you differ from the market, if you do. If you don't differ, say so explicitly -- 'no edge here, priced in' is a valid and useful conclusion.

self_qa.description: The adversarial layer. Modeled directly on the judge follow-ups in the Fed Challenge transcripts (e.g. 'what would have to change for you to think inflation was a bigger problem than the labor market'). Write these BEFORE you need them, not after the thesis breaks.

question.description: Ask yourself the hardest question a skeptical judge/PM would ask about this outlook.

falsification_trigger.description: The specific, checkable data print or event that would flip this view. Must be concrete -- 'if inflation stays high' is not a trigger, 'if 3mo annualized core PCE prints above 3.5% for two consecutive months' is.

trading_parameters.description: This is the interface to the per-ticker workflow -- the only part of this document other sessions/tabs actually need to consume programmatically.

calendar_effects_priority.description: Ranked list of which recurring calendar effects matter most right now, e.g. ['FOMC day', 'CPI print', 'NFP print'] -- ranking should shift with cycle phase (e.g. NFP matters more late-cycle when labor risk dominates).

event_vol_catalysts.description: Forward calendar of known catalysts feeding the event-vol straddle edge.

mean_reversion_window_confidence.description: Whether current regime supports trusting the standard mean-reversion backtest window, or whether it needs shortening/flagging given a regime change.

output_layers.description: Same underlying model, three different packagings for three different consumption moments -- don't re-derive, just re-render.

glance.description: Pre-market, <30 second read: regime tag + delta since last version only. What changed, nothing else.

narrative_ref.description: Pointer/filename to the full mock-FOMC-style writeup for this version (see economic_outlook_template.md).

trigger_feed.description: Event-driven one-liners generated on CPI/NFP/FOMC days: 'here's what just happened relative to what this outlook predicted.'

scorecard_log_ref.description: Pointer to the append-only scorecard log (see scorecard_log_template.json) where this version's calls get graded after the fact against what markets/tickers actually did.

current_reading.description: The actual current value/level. Always fill this from a real source at refresh time -- never carry a stale number forward silently.

role_in_outlook.description: What this reading implies for the regime call.

how_derived.description: MANDATORY, non-empty. The mechanism connecting the raw number to the conclusion. This is the single field the Fed Challenge dataset showed separates a good macro call from a cited-but-unexamined number. If you can't fill this in, the indicator doesn't belong in the outlook yet.

source.description: Where the reading came from (BLS, BEA, Fed H.15, NY Fed survey, etc.) and as-of date.

last_changed_meaningfully.description: Optional. Helps the 'glance' layer know whether this indicator is part of this version's delta.

trigger.description: Concrete, checkable condition -- same discipline as self_qa.falsification_trigger.

market_implication.description: What this would mean for the ticker-level workflow if it materializes -- sector/asset-class implications, not just macro commentary.
